limits: Gap 1: the lease proof requires every holder of AppState, its clients, observer or editor to be gone. A test local that outlives its app keeps the lease, so two looped tests were rescoped and one test drops references instead of tearing down. The proof polls an acquisition every 5 ms up to leaseCloseBound; that bound is a test bound, not a policy.

Gap 2: the logger drain no longer covers lines the artifact flush itself logs (observability.flush_timeout, the snapshot-unconfirmed line, the 'not fully confirmed' warning); nothing claims them. The immediate post-Quit assertion depends on the Quit's events drain confirming; .completed alone does not gate on allConfirmed. The reviewer's alternative (a second events flush with its own budget) was not adopted, per instruction.

Gap 3 DNS: the skip branch after a Stop (!admitsRunning, or a nil core) has no positive witness, because a skipping hop writes nothing. A stale old-core signal landing after a restart cannot be forced through production paths without a hook or a FIFO assumption. The guard is unchanged from R2. The test holds one owner turn with a bounded blocking wait while the pool resolves the queries, so it needs more than one pool thread. It therefore lives in RuntimePhysicalOrderingTests (focused and full runs), not in the strict filter.

Gap 3 sentinel witnesses: every hop publishes the state at landing, so the asserted value holds whichever hop replaced the sentinel. In practice the tests detect a regression to queued values, but that detection relies on the replacing hop being the stale one, which holds when the owner runs FIFO; correctness of the claim does not.

Auth P3: the tunnel-only test runs an unproxied tunnel so the tunnel lifecycle admits running, and calls reportAuthOutcome directly (the provider's outcome-handler entry). It is not a real proxied Kerberos handshake. The all-stopped no-spam negative is read after a measured bound (10x a fallback control hop's landing time, at least 100 ms), not a proof that both no-op hops ran. stopTunnels still does not clear lastAuthOutcome (existing behaviour; no owner choice made here). The R2 limit stands: a stale hop that lands after a stop and a new start can still publish the old run's outcome until the next report.

Gap 4: the row's tunnel start binds the fixed TunnelResolverPort 15053 on loopback, as the existing TunnelForwarderTests do. If another process holds that port, the row fails at 'the effect arrived'. No baseline control was executed against the pre-R2 pool-blocking manager, and none is claimed.

Gap 5: the held call is the teardown's networksetup subprocess on .platform-work, not a helper IPC call. The test asserts the total deadline, the closed stream, pendingAdmissions > 0 at return and the quit's end after release, now with main parked. It has no journal or lease assertion, and none was added (a lease assertion would be vacuous with a pinned lease).
